Connect

How other apps reach it, and what it reaches, in staging. Calls and subscriptions are granted here, not in the app's repository; the hosts outside the cluster it is granted are v2's, and this page shows them without offering to change them.

Allow callers
An app name, or team:<team> for every app of that team (its own team too: nothing is implicit); several comma-separated. Allowed in staging only. An app that calls demo-shop is connected once it is allowed.
It changes this instance only; granting access waits for you to merge it on GitHub.
Connect to an app
Apps it calls
No other web app in staging is left to call.
demo-shop gets each one's address and a short-lived token only that app accepts; each one starts admitting it. Any other app is blocked. Web apps in staging are offered; the catalogue shows each one's routes and each event's payload.
Events it receives
No other app in staging publishes an event it does not already receive.
demo-shop may read exactly these, from the oldest event still kept (seven days).
It changes this instance only; you review and merge it on GitHub, and a call connects once the app called allows it.

Call this from my app — what another app adds to reach demo-shop

A call needs both sides: your app calls demo-shop, and demo-shop allows your app or its team (Allow callers above). Use your app page's Connect to an app, or:

swhurl-v2 edit --records v2-records --app demo-shop --env staging --set allows=<whole list> \
  --profile v2/testdata/profile.json --out . --calls v2-records/calls.json --egress platform/egress/allocation.json
swhurl-v2 edit --records v2-records --app <your app> --env staging --set calls=<whole list> \
  --profile v2/testdata/profile.json --out . --calls v2-records/calls.json --egress platform/egress/allocation.json
swhurl-v2 render --records v2-records --profile v2/testdata/profile.json --out . --revision <commit>

Then, in your code (the stack templates' helper):

service("demo-shop").fetch("/")        // TypeScript
platform.call("demo-shop", "/")        // Kotlin
Subscribe to its events — what another app adds to receive them

Receiving events is granted on the platform, from your app page's Connect to an app, or:

swhurl-v2 edit --records v2-records --app <your app> --env staging --set subscriptions=<whole list> \
  --profile v2/testdata/profile.json --out . --calls v2-records/calls.json --egress platform/egress/allocation.json
swhurl-v2 render --records v2-records --profile v2/testdata/profile.json --out . --revision <commit>

Then, in your code:

subscribe("demo-shop.item-added", async (event) => { ... })        // TypeScript
events.subscribe("demo-shop.item-added") { event -> ... }            // Kotlin

Feature flags

An override changes a flag in staging at once, without a new image or a restart.

This console has no NATS key (console-nats Secret), so overrides cannot be read or set.

The image staging runs declares no feature flags. Declare them in the app's swhurl.yaml (how).

Change team
The team is the app's: the change moves staging and production together. It says who owns the app and whose notification channel hears about it; it grants nobody access, but a team: grant on another app follows it.
